gap_rows.title: rwb-integration rule copy: the H and C rows, the model-fetch surface, the assigned package, the local copy table, the event consumers and the login are not settled by any one source
gap_rows.source: WP B-P2-03; legacy RWB-E1-073 (sections 4, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 16); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG sections 3, 10, 12 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 20, 27, 28, 41, 43 row 30 and 44 JOB-20; Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16; FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7; TSD P2 Integration v3 T2; Plan Appendix R section R3 default ruling; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 (DP-01 to DP-19), R5.7 and R9
gap_rows.description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The plan sets Depends on (build) to None while the DP table adds eight H rows for the patterns this story applies, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), RWB-PLT-E1072-CON (DP-04), RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (DP-06), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10), RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (DP-14), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). (2) The contract-dependency row carries RWB-P3-E1073-CON while the DP-04 row names C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, and the model fetch is P7's operation. (3) Architecture v5 slide 43 row 30 names rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment as the consumers of RulePackageInForce while slide 20 says every service refreshes its cache on it; this story reads slide 20, which is what makes rwb-integration an evaluator, and the event payload beyond package code, version label, checksum and valid from is given nowhere. (4) The plan and the design decks name no package code assigned to rwb-integration, so the legacy ALLOCATION fixtures ALLOCATION, ALLOC-2026.11, ALLOC-2026.12, ALLOC-2026.13, TRF-2026.11, the rows ALLOC-014, ALLOC-015, ALLOC-031, ALLOC-032, ALLOC-040, ALLOC-041, ALLOC-999, the scenarios TA-07 and TA-19, the queues MTG-BKK-CO, MTG-UPC-CO, MTG-CEN-CO and GEN-CO, 24 and 26 rows, 50 scenarios, checksum 9f2c...e1b4 and valid from 2026-12-15 are used as synthetic test data only. (5) The model fetch is named GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} on Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 and appears in neither the Ownership Map nor API Specification v4, so its path segments and its request and response fields are unsettled. (6) The local copy table name and columns are given by no source, and the parameter read path and list code of the rwb-case contracts are equally unstated. (7) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login.
gap_rows.evidence: WP B-P2-03 story line for RWB-P2-E1073-APP ("H": [], "C": ["RWB-P3-E1073-CON"], patterns DP01 to DP19). Template and Rules v1 section R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, DP-06 adds H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, DP-10 adds H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-14 adds H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, DP-15 adds H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P2 rwb-integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, schema rwb_integration, topic rwb.integration.events.v1, queue rwb-integration, wave 1) and slide 20 (every service from the template: own schema with outbox, inbox and decision_record; RulePackageInForce to cache refresh). Slide 43 row 30 (RulePackageInForce consumers: rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment). Slides 14 and 27 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in; governance central, evaluation local, last good model kept). Slide 44 JOB-20 (rule promote 00:01, rwb-decision, Schedule to RulePackageInForce). Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16 (embedded kit, EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply per service queue, checksum before swap, KieBaseRegistry LRU max 20, first match writes the rule ID). FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7 step 1 ("Reads the version of the rules in force") and step 3 ("Writes the decision log entry"). TSD P2 Integration v3 T2 (IntegrationService "calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change"). Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 (five admin endpoints, no model fetch) and section 16 (twenty test cases, System and Access).
gap_rows.area: Rule package ownership, consumed contract rows and the local rule copy
gap_rows.proposed: Keep the plan's H and C lists as the story is written and record the eight DP H rows as wave-0 platform prerequisites in the Service Contract Catalog; publish the model fetch in RWB-P7-E1073-CON with the path, the request and the response fields agreed at the contract review; keep the ALLOCATION set as synthetic fixture data in the test environment only and replace it with the assigned package when the reference data names it; fix the local copy table, columns and migration in the rwb_integration DB story; name the login before the rwb_integration baseline is created.

asm_rows.text: The package code rwb-integration is assigned is named by no source, so the story is built and tested on the legacy ALLOCATION fixtures as synthetic test data: package ALLOCATION, versions ALLOC-2026.11, ALLOC-2026.12, ALLOC-2026.13 and TRF-2026.11, rows ALLOC-014, ALLOC-015, ALLOC-031, ALLOC-032, ALLOC-040, ALLOC-041 and ALLOC-999, scenarios TA-07 and TA-19, queues MTG-BKK-CO, MTG-UPC-CO, MTG-CEN-CO and GEN-CO, 24 and 26 rows, 50 scenarios, checksum 9f2c...e1b4 and valid from 2026-12-15. The assigned code, its version labels and its target queues are read at run time through the rwb-case reference-data contract and never appear in code.
asm_rows.why: Every DP-04 consuming story needs a package to load and evaluate, and neither the plan, the Ownership Map, the two design decks nor the legacy story names the package of rwb-integration; the legacy ALLOCATION values are the only ones the sources give, and inventing a code would be worse than reusing them as fixtures.
asm_rows.read: WP B-P2-03 story line; legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 7, 9 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 27; Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 16; RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 10 and its AC of the same shape.
asm_rows.confirm: Reference-data owner of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and the rwb-decision registry owner, before SIT
asm_rows.impact: A different assigned package changes fixtures and reference rows only; no behaviour, no code and no contract changes.

asm_rows.text: The model fetch is fixed for this run as GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel}, answering the model with its generated DRL, its state, its valid-from date, its SHA-256 checksum and the scenario set stored with the version, with 404 for an unknown label and 503 for an unavailable registry; the path segments, the request fields and the response fields are agreed with the rwb-decision owner at the contract review.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 name only GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and neither the Ownership Map nor API Specification v4 carries the operation, so a story cannot be built or contract-tested without a default; the placeholder alone would leave the client, the checksum check and the four fakes unspecified.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 27 and 41; Ownership Map v1 API rows (no rule-models operation); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 12.2 and 12.8 (the same sibling shape); Template and Rules v1 section R4 (base /api/recovery/<short>/v1).
asm_rows.confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P7-E1073-CON at the contract review, with the rwb-decision registry owner
asm_rows.impact: A renamed path or field touches one client, one fake and one section of this story; no business value changes.

asm_rows.text: The plan's dependency rows are followed as written: Depends on (build) is None, the contract dependency is RWB-P3-E1073-CON and there is no I or X row. The eight H rows the DP table adds (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are read as wave-0 platform prerequisites of the service template, the Drools kit and the workflow kit included, so the lane L-P2-D and the Day-1 start do not change; the DP-04 C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is the contract faked for the model fetch alongside the plan's RWB-P3-E1073-CON.
asm_rows.why: The plan and the DP table disagree on both the H rows and the C row, and a story cannot carry two dependency lists; the R-PREC order and the sibling slices of this same legacy key follow the plan's list, and treating the platform contracts as wave-0 prerequisites keeps the Day-1 rule of section R5.7 intact.
asm_rows.read: WP B-P2-03 story line; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4, R5.5 (DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.7; Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case to P7 under ASM-0069); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 13.
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect at the Service Contract Catalog review, with the platform and rwb-decision owners
asm_rows.impact: If the H rows become real build dependencies the lane waits for the wave-0 contract stories; the behaviour of the local load does not change.

asm_rows.text: The local copy lives in one table of rwb_integration created by migration V1073_1__local_rule_copy.sql, with a unique key on (package_code, version_label) and an index on the state, and holds the package code, version label, SHA-256 checksum, state, valid from, loaded at and the local run record of a refusal; the table name, the column names and the types are fixed by the rwb_integration DB story and are carried as "local model copy" until then.
asm_rows.why: No source names the local copy table or its columns, and DP-01 and DP-15 require the copy to be a table of this service's own schema written by its own Flyway sequence; leaving it unnamed would break the migration, the repository and the LRU restart behaviour of AC1 and AC5.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 13 (no new table; the registry tables are RWB-E1-072's); Architecture v5 slide 20 (own schema with decision_record) and slide 27 (each service holds its own approved copy); Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; Ownership Map v1 (outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key to PLT under ASM-0074).
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DB owner and the rwb_integration DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
asm_rows.impact: A different table or column set touches one migration, one repository and one section of this story; the behaviour is unchanged.

asm_rows.text: Architecture v5 slide 20 governs who consumes RulePackageInForce: every service refreshes its cache on it, so rwb-integration is an evaluator, despite slide 43 row 30 listing only rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment. The event carries the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 checksum and the valid-from date and nothing else, and is consumed with inbox dedupe, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt.
asm_rows.why: Two slides of the same catalogue disagree on the consumer list, and the payload is not published anywhere; a story cannot consume an event whose shape is open, and the sibling slices of this legacy key read slide 20.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service: RulePackageInForce to cache refresh) and slide 43 row 30 (four named consumers); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 15 (each owning service loads a version on RulePackageInForce); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.4.
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-decision event owner at the architecture review, before wave 1 build
asm_rows.impact: If the payload gains a field the consumer ignores it until the contract changes; if the consumer list were read instead, this service would have no rule copy and no local evaluation.

asm_rows.text: rules.testcases.min = 50 and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 are read on the business date through the parameters contract of rwb-case, under the legacy parameter codes of RWB-E1-042; the read path and the row identifiers of parameter_catalog and parameter_value are agreed with the rwb-case owner, and neither value is a constant, a values-file entry or a default in code.
asm_rows.why: DP-06 moves parameters to rwb-case and the plan sets no parameter dependency for this story; no source gives the target read path or the row identifiers, and the values themselves must not be written in code under BR12.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3 and 13 (rules.testcases.min = 50 assumed, drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06 and section R3 default ruling; Ownership Map v1 (parameter_catalog and parameter_value to P3); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: Parameter owner of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) before the contract review
asm_rows.impact: A changed value or row is data and needs no release; the story behaviour is unaffected.

asm_rows.text: MSG-P3-027 keeps the legacy text "The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}.", and the local load adds two {check} values to the six the legacy story fixes: checksum and package state, with {detail} naming the package, the two checksums, the state, the row, cell or scenario IDs and never a file payload or a personal value.
asm_rows.why: The legacy message enumerates compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario and stops there, while this slice refuses a load on the checksum and on the registry state before any of those run; no source gives the wording of the two added values or of the message prefix.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 14 (MSG-P3-027 and its {check} values); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 14; Error and Message Standard (prefix family); Architecture v5 slide 27 (verify checksum before swap).
asm_rows.confirm: Error and Message Standard owner, before the message catalogue is frozen
asm_rows.impact: One alert and one log text change; no behaviour changes.

asm_rows.text: The scenario set of a version travels in the model-fetch answer with the model: at least rules.testcases.min (50) cases, each with its facts, its expected queue or outcome and its scenario ID, so the local runner re-runs exactly the set that gated the version at rwb-decision. No second operation is added for it.
asm_rows.why: The design says the version's scenarios gate the load at rwb-decision and are stored with the version, while this slice must re-run them locally before the swap; no source says how they reach the service, and a second endpoint would add a contract this run cannot publish.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 4 and 13 (Rules tab, RuleScenarioRunner, rules.testcases.min); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 (50+ scenarios per version, checksum and DRL stored with it); Architecture v5 slide 27 (verify, swap, keep the last good model); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.4.
asm_rows.confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P7-E1073-CON at the contract review
asm_rows.impact: If the scenarios travel separately, the loader makes one more read with the same check; the refusal behaviour is unchanged.

asm_rows.text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed and carries it as a secret reference in the chart.
asm_rows.why: No source gives the login name and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login, which the target retires.
asm_rows.read: WP B-P2-03 story line; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 41 (one schema and one login per service); RWB-P2-E2001-APP section 3 (the same sibling default).
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
asm_rows.impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

asm_rows.text: The TSD P2 Integration v3 wording that IntegrationService "writes the decision log entry before any change" is read as the DP-03 one-transaction rule: the local decision record, the state change and the outbox row are written in one transaction in rwb_integration, and a failed record write leaves the change uncommitted instead of being written ahead of it.
asm_rows.why: The monolith wrote the log entry first because the log and the change sat behind separate calls; under DP-03 and R-UNI-39 the record and the change are one local transaction, and a separate write ahead of the change would leave a record of a change that never happened.
asm_rows.read: TSD P2 Integration v3 T2 (IntegrationService); FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7 step 3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28 (saved with the change, one transaction; strict mode); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14 (RecordAndApply, one transaction); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03.
asm_rows.confirm: Risk and Internal Audit at the ADR-009 and ADR-022 review, with the rwb-decision ledger owner
asm_rows.impact: A record written ahead of the change would need a compensating rule and a gap alert; the one-transaction reading keeps the legacy guarantee that nothing moves without a record.
